=== Trischettn Duel ===

Trischettn Duel is for two players: seat 1 is Player A, seat 2 is Player B. The deck has 32 cards in 4 suits (Hearts, Bells, Leaves, Acorns), 8 ranks each, from strongest to weakest: Ten (8), Nine (7), Ace (6), King (5), Ober (4), Unter (3), Eight (2), Seven (1). There are no trumps.

Pips: Ace 3; Ten 1, Nine 1, King 1, Ober 1, Unter 1; Eight 0, Seven 0. Winning the last (16th) trick of a deal gives 3 extra pips. Each deal holds 35 pips in total.

The match is exactly 2 deals of 16 tricks each, 32 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a deal: all cards are shuffled, each player gets 8 cards face down as a private hand, and the other 16 cards form the talon. Its top card is turned face up as 'talon up'. Both players' deal pips are set to 0. Seat 1 leads the first trick of deal 1, seat 2 leads the first trick of deal 2.

Each trick: the leader plays any one card from their hand face up. The follower then plays one card: if they hold any card of the led suit, they must play a card of that suit (only legal cards are offered); if they hold none, they may play any card. If both cards are of the led suit, the higher strength wins; otherwise (the follower did not follow suit) the leader wins. The winner adds the pips of both cards to their deal pips, plus 3 if it was the 16th trick. If the talon is not empty, the winner takes the face-up 'talon up' card into their hand (both players know it), the loser takes the next talon card face down (only the loser sees it), and if cards remain the new top card is turned face up as 'talon up', otherwise 'talon up' becomes 'none'. The talon empties after exactly 8 tricks; the last 8 tricks are played from hand with no drawing. The trick winner leads the next trick.

End of a deal: each player adds their deal pips to their match total.

After round 32, the higher match total (out of 70) wins. Equal totals (35 each) are a draw and both players share the win.

Trischettn Duel is for two players: seat 1 is Player A, seat 2 is Player B. The deck has 32 cards in 4 suits (Hearts, Bells, Leaves, Acorns), 8 ranks each, from strongest to weakest: Ten (8), Nine (7), Ace (6), King (5), Ober (4), Unter (3), Eight (2), Seven (1). There are no trumps.

The match is exactly 2 deals of 16 tricks each, 32 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a deal: all cards are shuffled, each player gets 8 cards face down as a private hand, and the other 16 cards form the talon. Its top card is turned face up as 'talon up'. Both players' deal pips are set to 0. Seat 1 leads the first trick of deal 1, seat 2 leads the first trick of deal 2.

Each trick: the leader plays any one card from their hand face up. The follower then plays one card: if they hold any card of the led suit, they must play a card of that suit (only legal cards are offered); if they hold none, they may play any card. If both cards are of the led suit, the higher strength wins; otherwise (the follower did not follow suit) the leader wins. === Trischettn Duel ===

Trischettn Duel is for two players: seat 1 is Player A, seat 2 is Player B. The deck has 32 cards in 4 suits (Hearts, Bells, Leaves, Acorns), 8 ranks each, from strongest to weakest: Ten (8), Nine (7), Ace (6), King (5), Ober (4), Unter (3), Eight (2), Seven (1). There are no trumps.

Pips: Ace 3; Ten 1, Nine 1, King 1, Ober 1, Unter 1; Eight 0, Seven 0. Winning the last (16th) trick of a deal gives 3 extra pips. Each deal holds 35 pips in total.

The match is exactly 2 deals of 16 tricks each, 32 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a deal: all cards are shuffled, each player gets 8 cards face down as a private hand, and the other 16 cards form the talon. Its top card is turned face up as 'talon up'. Both players' deal pips are set to 0. Seat 1 leads the first trick of deal 1, seat 2 leads the first trick of deal 2.

Each trick: the leader plays any one card from their hand face up. The follower then plays one card: if they hold any card of the led suit, they must play a card of that suit (only legal cards are offered); if they hold none, they may play any card. If both cards are of the led suit, the higher strength wins; otherwise (the follower did not follow suit) the leader wins. The winner adds the pips of both cards to their deal pips, plus 3 if it was the 16th trick. If the talon is not empty, the winner takes the face-up 'talon up' card into their hand (both players know it), the loser takes the next talon card face down (only the loser sees it), and if cards remain the new top card is turned face up as 'talon up', otherwise 'talon up' becomes 'none'. records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Trischettn Duel is for two players: seat 1 is Player A, seat 2 is Player B. The deck has 32 cards in 4 suits (Hearts, Bells, Leaves, Acorns), 8 ranks each, from strongest to weakest: Ten (8), Nine (7), Ace (6), King (5), Ober (4), Unter (3), Eight (2), Seven (1). There are no trumps.

Pips: Ace 3; Ten 1, Nine 1, King 1, Ober 1, Unter 1; Eight 0, Seven 0. Winning the last (16th) trick of a deal gives 3 extra pips. Each deal holds 35 pips in total.

The match is exactly 2 deals of 16 tricks each, 32 rounds in all; each round is one trick.

Start of a deal: all cards are shuffled, each player gets 8 cards face down as a private hand, and the other 16 cards form the talon. Its top card is turned face up as 'talon up'. Both players' deal pips are set to 0. Seat 1 leads the first trick of deal 1, seat 2 leads the first trick of deal 2.

Each trick: the leader plays any one card from their hand face up. The follower then plays one card: if they hold any card of the led suit, they must play a card of that suit (only legal cards are offered); if they hold none, they may play any card. If both cards are of the led suit, the higher strength wins; otherwise (the follower did not follow suit) the leader wins. The winner adds the pips of both cards to their deal pips, plus 3 if it was the 16th trick. If the talon is not empty, the winner takes the face-up 'talon up' card into their hand (both players know it), the loser takes the next talon card face down (only the loser sees it), and if cards remain the new top card is turned face up as 'talon up', otherwise 'talon up' becomes 'none'. The talon empties after exactly 8 tricks; the last 8 tricks are played from hand with no drawing. The trick winner leads the next trick.

End of a deal: each player adds their deal pips to their match total.

Both players see the deal and trick numbers, who leads, both cards of the current trick ('none' before they are played), the talon-up card or 'none', the number of cards left in the talon, and both players' deal pips and match totals. Each player sees only their own hand.

After round 32, the higher match total (out of 70) wins. Equal totals (35 each) are a draw and both players share the win.
